candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis specifies Trichophyton interdigitale as the causative agent. The candidate states Trichophyton mentagrophytes. Although the mycological culture report in the clinical record uses the older name 'T. mentagrophytes', modern molecular taxonomy (ITS and D1/D2 LSU sequencing, also performed here) distinguishes T. interdigitale (the zoophilic/anthropophilic species associated with animal contact, including cats) from T. mentagrophytes sensu stricto. The reference reflects the updated taxonomic assignment confirmed by sequence analysis, while the candidate retains the superseded species name, constituting an incompatible subtype designation at the species level.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Species-level taxonomic conflict: T. mentagrophytes vs T. interdigitale

case_quality_flags: Taxonomic ambiguity: clinical record uses legacy name 'T. mentagrophytes' in culture report, but sequence analysis was performed and reference applies current taxonomy (T. interdigitale); reviewers should note this nomenclature evolution when assessing candidates
